title: Restore Us to Yourself: Lamentations 4-5, Song of Songs 8, John 7, 1 Peter 5
summary: Lamentations 4-5 finished the book: chapter 4 as the third eikah poem, a shorter single acrostic with pe (4:16, 'the face of the Lord') before ayin (4:17, 'our eyes failed'); chapter 5 as a 22-line non-acrostic communal prayer rhyming on -nu (us/our), titled 'the prayer of Jeremiah' in old versions. Covered: precious sons as earthen pots (Jer 19), the ostrich mothers (Henry paraphrased), worse than Sodom (Henry 'by inches', Carson on degrees of guilt), 4:10 bashal with 2 Kings 6:29 and Deuteronomy 28 (Calvin on 'compassionate'), prophets and priests as lepers (Lev 13:45) with Poole's quote on a godly versus corrupt ministry, Egypt's false hope (Jer 37), Zedekiah caught at Jericho (Jer 39). Hard question one, 4:20 'breath of our nostrils': Zedekiah honored for the office (Calvin), the LXX 'Christ the Lord' read by the fathers (Irenaeus quoted on the trodden shadow), and Calvin's 'we must come to Christ, who is really ... the breath of our nostrils' as NT move one. 4:21-22 Edom in Uz and 'accomplished' (tam) answered the comfort thread with Isaiah 40:2 (Ellicott), Henry's 'designed' limit, and Spurgeon's sermon 480 on Christ bearing the punishment as NT move two. Chapter 5: 'our mothers are like widows' (5:3) closed the like thread; 5:7 versus 5:16 (Keil and Delitzsch paraphrased); 5:19 equals Psalm 102:12 (Calvin's 'hundred times' paraphrased). Hard question two, the ending: ki im options, Calvin's 'unless' ('it is singular that no one has perceived this'), the synagogue custom of repeating 5:21 (Calvin 'superstition', Henry 'sun may not set under a cloud', Gerlach's morning star via Keil and Delitzsch), the shuv wordplay matching Jeremiah 31:18, Calvin (not repentance) versus Henry ('Turn us or we shall not be turned', quoted) with Augustine on Psalm 80 and effectual calling; application: ask first to be restored to God himself. Song 8:8-14: the brothers of 1:6, wall and door (Keil and Delitzsch versus Durham), 'I was a wall' and shalom/Shelomoh, Cambridge versus Keil and Delitzsch on the brothers' credit, Jerome's Letter 107 noted, application to fathers of daughters; Baal-hamon 'lord of a multitude' and rented versus given love; 8:13 with Spurgeon sermon 1716 ('You talk to everybody but to Me'); 8:14 barach, Bether versus spices, Durham's 'uninterrupted communion is reserved for heaven', and Revelation 22:20 (Spurgeon, Gill). John 7:25-36: the Jerusalemites, the hidden-Messiah belief (Justin's Trypho) against 7:42 Bethlehem, Calvin's 'mangle ... Christ himself' on reading half of Micah 5:2, ekraxen as bridge to 7:37, alethinos, 7:30 the hour (Augustine 'not born under fate' quoted; Calvin's decree; Henry's 'God ties their hands'), officers previewed for 7:45-46, 7:33-34 too late (Henry's pillar of cloud, Cyril's Opportunity) balanced by Augustine on Pentecost pardon, and diaspora (7:35; James 1:1; 1 Peter 1:1). 1 Peter 5:8-14 finished the letter: nepho a third time, gregoreo and Gethsemane, antidikos and diabolos, the two lions with Lamentations 3:10 (Leighton quoted), Brooks's 'safe to resist, dangerous to dispute', Spurgeon 1861 'worry but cannot rend', katartizo (mending nets) and sterizo (Luke 22:32), Silvanus, Babylon as Rome (Eusebius; host's view) versus literal Babylon (Calvin, Poole, Henry, Gill), Mark restored. Close: diaspora mocked in John 7:35 became Peter's addressees; Lamentations 5:21's prayer answered by 1 Peter 5:10's promise; Calvin's last Lamentations lecture line about beginning Ezekiel tomorrow.
threads: Lamentations, the Song of Songs and 1 Peter are finished. The like thread (1:1 widow, 2:5 enemy, 3:10 bear and lion, 5:3 mothers like widows) and the comfort thread (1:2, 2:13, 3:21-24, 4:22 with Isaiah 40:2) are closed.

Ezekiel 1-3 is next and needs a book introduction: Ezekiel the priest among the exiles at the Chebar canal, carried off with Jehoiachin in 597 (Jeremiah 52 and the ration tablets were taught in episode 9), the thirtieth year and fifth year of Jehoiachin's exile (593 B.C.), the throne-chariot vision, the scroll eaten (compare Jeremiah 15:16 and the scrolls of Jeremiah 36 and 51), and the watchman (3:17). Calvin lectured on Ezekiel 1-20 right after Lamentations; his line 'I will begin tomorrow the explanation of Ezekiel' was used today. Ezekiel 18 (sour grapes) will pick up Lamentations 5:7.

Job 1 is next and starts a new book: 'There was a man in the land of Uz' links to Lamentations 4:21 (Edom dwelling in Uz; Gill places Job's Uz near Edom). Needs an introduction: setting, date debates (patriarchal setting, traditional view), prose frame and poetic core, the accuser (ha-satan) in 1:6, which links to today's 1 Peter 5:8 adversary. Brooks's 'Job resists, and conquers upon the dunghill' was used today.

2 Peter 1:1-11 starts a new letter: Simeon Peter, 'his divine power has granted to us all things', partakers of the divine nature, the ladder of virtues, 'make your calling and election sure'. Tie to 1 Peter 5:10's 'called you to his eternal glory'.

John 7:37-44 is next: the last day, the great day of the feast, the water-pouring ceremony (Mishnah Sukkah in an earlier research file; Ellicott fetched), Jesus 'cried out' (ekraxen again, set up today), rivers of living water and the Spirit, and the division over Bethlehem (7:42, set up today against 7:27). The officers return in 7:45-46 with 'No one ever spoke like this man' (Spurgeon sermon 951 'The Unrivalled Eloquence of Jesus' fetched).

Unused today: Calvin's 'every man would contrive an offense for himself' and 'Bethlehem ... a door', Ryle's 'They are immortal, till their work is done' and 'finding out truth too late', MacArthur's 'Hell is not where Christ is forgotten; it is where He is unavailable', Westcott on alethinos and Captivity versus Dispersion, Chrysostom's 'words of drunken men', Sproul on the neglected ascension (7:33); Leighton's pirates and 'drunken soldier', Gurnall on sobriety, Spurgeon's 'big black dog' and ship, Piper's 'not the God of some grace' (Solid Joys), Spurgeon Morning and Evening July 11 (gnarled oak), MacLaren on Silvanus; Henry's 'One word of Christ before you part' (Ussher) and 'Why tarry the wheels of his chariots?', Hudson Taylor on Bether, Ambrose on 8:9-10; Calvin on 4:17 and 5:19, Henry on 4:20 (creature as breath; Jonah's gourd), James Smith on 4:20, Justin's cross-shaped face, Ligonier 'A Final Plea for Restoration', Carson 5:21.

Voices quoted this episode: Poole, Irenaeus, Calvin (4 quotes: Lamentations 4:20, 5:22, Ezekiel line, John 7:27), Spurgeon (sermons 480 and 1716), Henry, Durham, Augustine, Leighton, Brooks. Paraphrased: Henry (several), Carson, Keil and Delitzsch, Ellicott, Cambridge, Jerome, Justin, Cyril, Eusebius, Spurgeon 419. Desiring God still returns 403 for sermons; the Solid Joys page loaded. No Sproul on today's passages except a John 7:32-52 sermon transcript (unused).

show_notes: Lamentations ends on its knees: 'Restore us to yourself, O Lord... unless you have utterly rejected us.' We close three books today, with the breath of our nostrils captured at Jericho, a wall and a door in the Song, the crowd arguing over where the Messiah comes from, and Peter, once asleep in Gethsemane, telling the churches to watch for the roaring lion.
